previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic gastroparesis was admitted for a flare of epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting, with a blood glucose over 700 mg/dL. She had stopped her sliding scale insulin due to poor intake and fear of hypoglycemia. Her pain improved with Dilaudid and lidocaine patch, and she was able to tolerate oral intake. A gastric emptying study confirmed delayed gastric emptying. Her insulin regimen was adjusted with an increase in nighttime Lantus to 14 units. Hypertension improved with restart of home medications. She developed pseudohyponatremia, which resolved with better glycemic control. PTH was elevated, prompting initiation of vitamin D. Despite ongoing hyperglycemia, she chose to be discharged home to care for her son, with a follow-up appointment scheduled in the diabetes clinic the next day. Port placement was deferred to outpatient setting.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ w/T1DM c/b gastroparesis, ESRD on HD 
presenting with abdominal pain, N/V and found to have glucose 
>1300. 

#HYPEROSMOLAR HYPERGLYCEMIC STATE: By glucose >600, pH>7.3, 
bicarb>15. Trigger was thought to be most likely volume 
depletion and oral intolerance leading to non-compliance with 
treatment. She was addditionally worked up for an infectious 
etiology of her HHS, which was unrevealing.  An EKG demonstrated 
no ischemic changes and she had no chest discomfort on 
presentation.  She was initially treated with an insulin gtt 
which was ultimately stopped on ___. ___ Diabetes 
specialists were consulted for assistance and recommended 
increasing her evening ___ dose to 7u.  They continued to 
follow her after she was called out to the floor. Glucose was 
difficult to control during her time on the medicine floor with 
finger stick glucose levels ranging from 37 to >500. She did 
develop a gap although there was no evidence of any serum 
ketones. ___ continued to follow Ms. ___ and ___ 
dose continued to be increased. At the time of discharge her 
___ dose was 8 units with breakfast and 10 units with dinner. 
She was also advised to continue the insulin sliding scale with 
4 units of Humalog with meals and use of a correction scale of 1 
unit of insulin for every 50 over 150. At the time of discharge, 
her finger stick glucose continued to be in the 400s. Her last 
serum glucose obtained in the hospital was 363. She was advised 
to follow-up with her endocrinologist at ___, Dr. 
___ for further follow-up and management of her 
diabetes.  

#TROPONEMIA: Likely reflects demand ischemia in the setting of 
frequent hypertension compounded by poor renal clearance, with 
low suspicion for ACS. Cardiac biomarkers downtrended without 
further intervention. She did not have any chest pain, chest 
pressure, or shortness of breath during hospitalization.  

#GASTROPARESIS FLARE: Per OMR patient has diabetic gastroparesis 
with recurrent flares. She was given Zofran as needed to help 
with nausea.  She additionally received Tylenol and 
Hydromorphone at 1mg IV q4hrs for severe pain.  She was able to 
tolerate a diet.  On the floor her abdominal pain resolved and 
hydromorphone was discontinued. She had a good appetite and was 
able to tolerate meals without further nausea or vomiting.  

#ESRD: Patient has ESRD secondary to Type I Diabetes.  She is on 
hemodialysis ___. She continued 
hemodialysis per her outpatient regimen with our dialysis team 
without any difficulties.  

#HYPERTENSION: Elevated in setting of acute medical 
decompensation. Patient reports that her normal SBP is in the 
180.  In the setting of acute illness, her Labetalol was dosed 
at 200mg TID rather than 400mg TID. Her blood pressure continued 
to be in the 180s. We subsequently titrated her labetalol dose 
up to 400 mg TID, with improvement of her blood pressure with 
SBP in the 140s. 

#ACCESS: Ms. ___ has been hospitalized numerous times in the 
past for complications of her diabetes. During her 
hospitalizations she has difficult intravenous access. As a 
result, she underwent a Left internal jugular approach chest 
single lumen Port-a-cath placement. This procedure was 
successful and she was discharge with good intravenous access 
for the future.

Findings paged to the covering house officer, Dr. ___,
at the time of discovery of 10:10 a.m. on the day of the exam and discussed
with him by Dr. ___ by telephone shortly thereafter.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with type I diabetes mellitus, ESRD on
hemodialysis (RUE fistula), diabetic gastroparesis who has difficult
peripheral access requiring port placement. Multiple prior presentations with
diabetic ketoacidosis requiring resuscitation.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and
Dr. ___ radiology attending) performed the procedure. The
attending, Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
75mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 30 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl and midazolam. 1 g of cefazolin.

CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 3.6 min, 3 mGy

PROCEDURE
1. Left internal jugular approach chest single lumen Port-a-cath placement

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The upper chest was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the left internal jugular vein was
compressible with moderate echogenic clot on the medial wall (suggestive of a
chronic clot) accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent ultrasound
images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which confirmed vein
patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right atrium using
fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.
The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was advanced to make
appropriate measurements for catheter length. The ___ wire was then passed
distally into the IVC.

Next, attention was turned towards creation of a subcutaneous pocket over the
upper anterior chest wall. After instilling superficial and deeper local
anesthesia using lidocaine mixed with epinephrine, a 2.5 cm transverse
incision was made and a subcutaneous pocket was created by using blunt
dissection. The single lumen port was then connected to the catheter. The
catheter was tunneled from the subcutaneous pocket towards the venotomy site
from where it was brought out using a tunneling device. The port was then
connected to the catheter and checks were made for any leakage by accessing
the diaphragm using a non-coring ___ needle. No leaks were found.
The port was then placed in the subcutaneous pocket and secured with ___
Prolene sutures on either side. The venotomy tract was dilated using the
introducer of the peel-away sheath supplied. Following this, the peel-away
sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the port was threaded into
the right side of the heart with the tip in the right atrium. The sheath was
then peeled away.
The subcutaneous pocket was closed in layers with ___ interrupted and ___
subcuticular continuous Vicryl sutures. ___ Vicryl suture and Steri-Strips
were used to close the venotomy incision site. Steri-Strips were applied over
the sutures. Final spot fluoroscopic image demonstrating good alignment of the
catheter and no kinking. The tip is in the right atrium.
The port was accessed using a non coring ___ needle and could be aspirated
and flushed easily. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient tolerated the
procedure well without immediate complication. The port was  left accessed as
requested.

FINDINGS: 

Chronic Medium-sized clot in the medial wall of the left IJ.  Final
fluoroscopic image showing port with catheter tip terminating in the right
atrium.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a single lumen chest Port-a-cath via the left internal
jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter terminates in the right
atrium. The catheter is ready for use.

Chronic medium-sized o'clock in the medial wall of the left IJ.
